messages:
Maya (PM): Heads-up: a competitor rolled out per-route SLOs + automatic regional failover overnight. A couple of prospects asked if we can match it. Need a quick product decision.

Kevin (Eng): Saw it. Their implementation looks like per-tenant SLO plumbing + routing fallback. Feasible, but touches routing plane, KV cache coherence, and infra automation. Recommend a short technical spike.

Sasha (Design): From interviews, customers want a tiny, confident control: one latency target and an opinionated default. Avoid exposing a hundred toggles at launch.

Liam (Sales): Two active opportunities (one healthcare, one fintech) called this out explicitly in RFPs. If we can show a credible ETA, I can stall procurement pushes.

Aria (Data): I'll pull per-route p95 by region for the last 7 days and surface which routes would benefit most from failover.

Elena (CTO): Quick note: if we chase parity, we must not accrue hidden infra debt. Spike should include failover simulation and cost modeling.

Maya (PM): Proposed approach: 2-sprint spike (feasibility + key risk tests) -> 2-sprint MVP (API + runtime + basic telemetry) -> iterate console/UX later. Timeline estimate ~6 weeks.

Kevin (Eng): MVP sketch:
- API: PATCH /routes/{id}/slo { p95_ms: 150 }
- Runtime: per-route region preference + deterministic fallback
- Telemetry: per-route p95, failover events, error-rate
- Ops: alerts when SLO missed >5m and manual rollback hook
No advanced UI for initial rollout; accept via API/console flag.

Sasha (Design): I'll mock a one-line Routes entry (latency target + info tooltip) and a simple canary banner. Keep copy that sets expectations about limited-region rollout.

Maya (PM): Resourcing ask for spike: 1 backend, 1 infra, 0.5 designer for 2 sprints. Conditional MVP if spike shows no fatal infra issues.

Liam (Sales): That resourcing is reasonable. If you give me a 6-8 week ETA, I can push for LOIs on those two deals with a canary SLA clause.

Aria (Data): Early telemetry: some routes show 40-90ms p95 variance across regions. Failover could materially reduce SLA breaches for those routes. I'll attach a draft dashboard later today.

Elena (CTO): Also consider Private deployment implications: KMS and network policy during cross-region failover need verification. Include a short checklist in the spike.

Kevin (Eng): Spike will focus on cache sync strategies, routing state handoff, and KMS behavior in Private mode. I'll post a 72-hour spike plan in this thread.

Maya (PM): Tradeoffs for leadership:
- Pros: meeting parity unlocks near-term revenue and reduces churn risk for enterprise
- Cons: diverts engineering from Optimize features that lower unit cost
We should decide tactical parity vs staying on cost-effort path.

Sasha (Design): Product narrative must remain centered on our differentiators (model-level routing, cost controls). Frame this parity as enterprise guardrails, not a product pivot.

Maya (PM): Action items:
- Kevin: start spike and share a 72-hour plan + estimate within 3 working days
- Aria: publish 7-day telemetry + dashboard mock by EOD
- Sasha: create minimal Routes UI mock + copy for canary
- Liam: draft LOI-friendly canary SLA language for customers

Kevin (Eng): Starting spike now. Will post findings and any blockers in this thread.

prod-bot: Ticket PROD-5421 created: "Spike - per-route SLO & regional failover" assigned to Kevin.

Maya (PM): Great. Quick sync Friday to decide go/no-go on MVP. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
